1.explanation:
• TableBatchActions.js is the React wrapper that shows/hides the batch action bar and currently applies a translateX to slide it in; if the inner list can’t scroll fully left, left‐hand buttons remain hidden.
• TableActionList.js renders the <ul> of individual batch actions and should support full horizontal scrolling; it needs className or style tweaks to enable that on small viewports.
• TableToolbar.js is the parent container that applies overflow‐hidden and positioning around TableBatchActions; it may need adjustments to allow its child to overflow/scroll correctly.
• The SCSS partial _action.scss in styles/scss/components/data-table/action defines the CSS rules (overflow, white-space, flex) for the batch action list; it must be updated to permit horizontal scrolling and remove hard clipping on narrow screens.
1.bug_scenario: When you select rows on a narrow viewport (mobile or small desktop) the batch‐action bar at the top of the DataTable slides in as expected but its leftmost buttons (e.g. “Download to” or “Test 1”) are clipped off. The horizontal overflow container never scrolls far enough to expose those first actions, so you can’t tap them on small screens.

2.explanation:
• TableBatchActions.js: This is the React wrapper that shows or hides the batch-action bar and wires up the next/previous scroll controls. Any fix to enable scrolling or to change when those controls appear must start here.  

• TableActionList.js: This component actually renders the list of actions inside the batch-actions bar. Its flexbox settings and prop-getter logic determine whether the items can shrink or overflow. Adjusting the item flex rules here (for example, adding `flex: 0 0 auto`) or modifying how the scroll buttons are triggered will be required.  

• styles/scss/components/data-table/action/_action.scss: The core styles for batch actions in the `styles` package define the container’s `overflow`, `white-space` and hidden-scroll behavior. They currently clip off items when the container width is smaller than the total button width. You’ll need to amend these rules (for example, ensuring `overflow-x: auto` and visible scroll bars or adding a `min-width` to buttons) so that all items remain reachable.  

• packages/carbon-react/src/scss/components/data-table/action/_action.scss: The Carbon React distribution also ships its own SCSS overrides for DataTable batch actions. Any end-user who relies on the SCSS in `carbon-react` will need the same adjustments here to match changes in the core `styles` layer.
2.bug_scenario: When you select rows in a DataTable and switch to a smaller viewport (for example on mobile or narrow windows), the batch-action buttons (rendered by <TableBatchActions>) no longer fit: the first few actions are clipped off to the left and there is no way to scroll to them. In the screenshot you can see the “Download to” button (the first item) partially hidden behind the left edge, while the rest of the actions remain accessible. The scrolling logic and/or CSS overflow settings in <TableBatchActions> and the underlying action-list container aren’t kicking in on small screens, so the user can’t reach those early buttons.
